subject: Political Science
central_question: How did the political, economic and constitutional conflicts of the mid-1970s lead to the Emergency, and what did this episode reveal about the strengths and weaknesses of Indian democracy?
in_scope_units: Background to Emergency: political polarisation, economic distress and growing dissatisfaction after 1971.
Gujarat and Bihar movements: student protests, Jayaprakash Narayan and the call for Total Revolution.
Railway Strike of 1974: labour unrest, workers’ rights and the government response.
Conflict with Judiciary: disputes over Fundamental Rights, constitutional amendments and the Kesavananda Bharati case.
Declaration of Emergency: the Allahabad High Court judgment, political confrontation and invocation of Article 352.
Consequences: censorship, preventive detention, suspension of rights, constitutional amendments and resistance.
Lessons of the Emergency: civil liberties, institutional safeguards and the tension between protest and governance.
Politics after Emergency: the 1977 election, formation of the Janata Party and defeat of the Congress.
Janata Government and Legacy: instability, return of Congress in 1980 and long-term changes in the party system.
banned_topics: Detailed history of regional autonomy movements, which belongs to the chapter on Regional Aspirations.
Detailed post-1989 coalition politics and Mandal politics, which belong to the chapter on Recent Developments in Indian Politics.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Emergency was imposed only because economic conditions had worsened.
known_pitfalls.correction: Economic distress formed part of the background, but the immediate political confrontation followed the Allahabad High Court judgment, opposition demands for Indira Gandhi’s resignation and the government’s claim of a threat from internal disturbances.

known_pitfalls.claim: All democratic institutions completely disappeared during the Emergency.
known_pitfalls.correction: Normal democratic politics was severely curtailed, rights were suspended and censorship imposed, but the Emergency was later withdrawn and elections were held in 1977, restoring democratic functioning.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Congress was defeated uniformly across India in 1977.
known_pitfalls.correction: The anti-Congress wave was strongest in north India, while the Congress retained many seats in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Orissa and performed strongly in the southern States.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 6 to analyse the reasons officially given for declaring the Emergency.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to compare the Emergency’s effects on civil liberties, the judiciary, the media, and the police and bureaucracy.
Use NCERT Exercise 7 to explain why the opposition won power at the Centre in 1977.
Use NCERT Exercise 9 to trace how the Emergency changed India’s party system.
Use NCERT Exercise 10 to examine why the 1977 party system appeared close to a two-party system.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with an EXERCISES section containing Questions 1–10.
